'''Mangala Narlikar''' (17 May 1943 – 17 July 2023) was an Indian mathematician who did research in [[pure mathematics]] as well as writing for a lay audience. After her degrees in mathematics, she initially worked at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) in [[Mumbai]] and later worked as a lecturer in the University of Bombay and Pune.

==Biography==
Narlikar was born as Mangala Rajwade<ref name="Murty 2008 p. 30">{{cite book | last=Murty | first=K.K. | title=50 Timeless Scientists | publisher=Pustak Mahal | year=2008 | isbn=978-81-223-1030-6 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WX9r7TAaWgEC&pg=PT30 | access-date=17 July 2023 | page=30}}</ref> on 17 May 1943<ref name="Bengrut 2023 j334">{{cite web | last=Bengrut | first=Dheeraj | title=Eminent mathematician Dr Mangala Narlikar passes away at 80 | website=Hindustan Times | date=17 July 2023 | url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/eminent-mathematician-dr-mangala-narlikar-passes-away-at-80-101689579959114.html | access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> in [[Bombay]], [[Bombay Presidency|Bombay Province]], as the place was known during the [[British India]] era.<ref name="Free Press Journal 2023 r732">{{cite web | title=Pune: Renowned Mathematician Mangala Jayant Narlikar Passes Away At 80 | website=Free Press Journal | date=17 July 2023 | url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/pune/pune-renowned-mathematician-mangala-jayant-narlikar-passes-away-at-80 | access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> She studied from the University of Bombay and received degrees of B. A. (Maths) in 1962 and M.A. (Maths) in 1964 with first rank and also won the Chancellor's gold medal.<ref name=Fund/>{{Sfn|Chengalvarayan|Gokilvani|2007|p=110}} She married, [[Jayant Narlikar]], a well known cosmologist and physicist, in 1966. They have three daughters, Geeta, Girija and Leelavati, all of whom have pursued careers in science; one (Geeta) is a professor of biochemistry at the [[University of California, San Francisco]], and the other two are in computer science.<ref name="Legend">{{cite journal |last1=Dadhich |first1=Naresh |title=Living Legends in Indian Science {{!}} Jayant Vishnu Narlikar |date=10 July 2014 |access-date=17 July 2023 |journal=[[Current Science]] |volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=113–120 |jstor=24103414 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/24103414 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717123616/https://www.jstor.org/stable/24103414 |archive-date=17 July 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref><ref name=Cosmo>{{Cite web|url=http://brainprick.com/mangala-narlikar-the-journey-of-an-informal-mathematician/|title=Mangala Narlikar: The Journey of an Informal Mathematician: Academic Featured Biographies|date=9 July 2012|access-date=1 November 2015|publisher=Brainprick|archive-date=21 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121043443/http://brainprick.com/mangala-narlikar-the-journey-of-an-informal-mathematician/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
  
From 1964 to 1966, Narlikar worked as a Research Student and Research Associate in the School of Mathematics of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. From 1967 to 1969, she taught the undergraduate school  at the University of Cambridge. From 1974 to 1980 she again worked in the School of Mathematics of TIFR.<ref name=Fund/> She obtained her Ph.D. degree  in mathematics from the University of Bombay, 16 years after her marriage,<ref name=Wist>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/cen/books/87/8703books.html|title=Indian Women In Science|access-date=1 November 2015|date=19 January 2009|first1=Vijaysree |last1=Venkatraman |website=Chemical & Engineering News |publisher=American Chemical Society}}</ref> in 1981 on the subject of [[analytic number theory]].{{Sfn|Chengalvarayan|Gokilvani|2007|p=110}} After obtaining her doctoral degree, she continued to work with TIFR from 1982 to 1985 as a Pool Officer in the School of Mathematics. Her teaching assignments from 1982 to 1985 was for M Phil class in the Department of Mathematics in the University of Bombay. She also taught at intervals in the Department of Mathematics at the University of Pune from 1989 to 2002 and taught M Sc students at the centre in Bhaskaracharya Pratishthan from 2006 to 2010.<ref name=Fund>{{Cite web|url=http://elearning.bprim.org/speaker/profile/dr-mangala-narlikar|title=E-learning in Mathematics at Undergraduate and Postgraduate Level|access-date=1 November 2015|publisher=Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140420130033/http://elearning.bprim.org/speaker/profile/dr-mangala-narlikar|archive-date=20 April 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Narlikar's core fields of interest were real and complex analysis, analytic geometry, number theory, algebra, and topology.<ref name=Fund/>

On writing books on mathematics, Narlikar wrote: "I enjoyed writing a book on how to make mathematics interesting and accessible".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imsc.res.in/~jniyer/talkAjit.pdf|title= What Science Academies do for Indian Women in Mathematics|access-date=1 November 2015|publisher=The Institute of Mathematical Sciences}}</ref> On her combining her profession with looking after the household functions she wrote: "My story is perhaps a representation of the lives of many women of my generation who are well educated but always put household responsibilities before their personal careers".<ref name=Cosmo/> She was chairman of mathematics subject committee for Maharashtra State Bureau of Textbook Production and Curriculum Research.

Mangala Narlikar died of cancer on 17 July 2023, at the age of 80.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eminent mathematician Dr Mangala Narlikar dies at 80 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/eminent-mathematician-dr-mangala-narlikar-dies-at-80-8843281/ |access-date=17 July 2023 |publisher=The Indian Express |date=17 July 2023}}</ref>

==Publications==
Narlikar published a number of scientific papers and books which included:<ref name=Fund/>

===Papers=== 
*''Theory of Sieved Integers'', Acta Arithmetica 38, 157 in 19
* ''On a [[Erdős–Szemerédi theorem|theorem of Erdos and Szemeredi]]'', Hardy Ramanujan Journal 3, 41, in 1980
*''On the Mean Square Value theorem of Hurwitz Zeta function'', Proceedings of Indian Academy of Sciences 90, 195, 1981.
*''Hybrid mean Value Theorem of L-functions'', Hardy Ramanujan  Journal 9, 11 - 16, 1986.
*''On orders solely of Abelian Groups'',  Bulletin of London  Mathematical Society, 20, 211 - 216, in 1988.
* several articles on mathematics in Science Age, to create interest in mathematics among lay people

===Books===
* ''Ganitachyaa Sopya Vata'', a book in Marathi for schoolchildren
*''An Easy Access to Basic Mathematics'', a book for schoolchildren.
*''A Cosmic Adventure'', translation of a book on Astronomy by Professor J. V. Narlikar.
